why: Exit 1 is a non-blocking error: the call goes ahead. A refusal is exit 2. Mark a real non-refusal with a `not a refusal` comment on its line.
bad:
if grep -q "rm -rf" "$cmd"; then
  echo "BLOCKED" >&2
  exit 1
fi
good:
if grep -q "rm -rf" "$cmd"; then
  echo "BLOCKED" >&2
  exit 2
fi
test -f x || exit 1  # not a refusal: a usage error
